key_insight: ProDiT is a multimodal diffusion model that generates diverse proteins conditioned on desired functions, including proteins with multiple structural states. The reported functions are computationally predicted, not established here through experimental validation.
problem_solved: Generative protein design needs to go beyond producing individual structures to designing diverse proteins with targeted functions and multiple states.
method: Uses multimodal diffusion to generate protein designs.
Conditions generation on desired protein functions.
Supports multistate protein generation rather than only single-state designs.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, ProDiT illustrates how multimodal diffusion can extend scientific generation toward functional constraints and multistate outputs. It points toward more flexible protein-design workflows, while computational predictions still require experimental confirmation.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: desired function → ProDiT → generated protein candidates.
One protein shown in multiple conformations to explain multistate design.
Gallery of varied protein shapes to illustrate design diversity.
Evidence-status badge: computationally predicted function ≠ experimentally validated function.
paper_title: Generating proteins with computationally predicted functions and multiple states via multimodal diffusion
paper_authors: Bowen Jing, Anna Sappington, Mihir Bafna, Ravi Shah, Adrina Tang
